wakeReasons: unread diplomatic messages or new offers
own alliance or enemy relations change
own industry loss of at least max(3, quarter of last planned industry)

primaryEndpoint: paired final own industry, hybrid minus baseline; eight country/seed pairs
secondaryEndpoints: Jeff input tokens, local latency and API fees (zero; CPU hosting cost unknown)
accepted diplomacy and message counts (not reply-quality or response-delay measures)

analysis.industry: exact two-sided sign-flip plus exploratory 10000 paired bootstrap resamples
analysis.cost: actual usage by token category and local Jeff inference latency; Goodwin hosting price is unknown, never treat SDK zero placeholders as billing
analysis.missing: retain every attempt; never count incomplete games as losses or mix pilots into strength evidence

constraints: Only two main arms requested by user
Separate authenticated loopback rooms, ordinary HTTP validation
Normal speed, seven unchanged practice bots
Freeze game rules, map and controller before main launch
Preserve speech as untrusted data; use only inbox metadata for wake decisions
No fallback controller counted as Jeff
Healthy local CPU Jeff preflight before starting any comparison rooms
Independent durable research workers; never touch live service or deploy worktree
limitations: Plans and game trajectories may diverge
This compares whole systems: planner scheduling and military interface change
Hybrid menu restricts offensive sources to bordering provinces and lacks army turn-around
Bots do not reproduce human diplomacy
Goodwin hosting dollars cannot be inferred from token counts
Concurrent cases share the CPU selector and Goodwin endpoint; latency under load differs from single-game service time.
Offer/message response delays are not recorded comparably by the baseline; no prompt diplomatic responsiveness claim.

localRuntime.deployment: one decision service, no GPU allocation
localRuntime.concurrency: eight matched blocks concurrently, baseline/hybrid launch order alternates; shared model service load is part of these measurements
localRuntime.busyPolicy: retry HTTP 529 with jitter until 120 second deadline; measure queue-inclusive and successful request server latency separately
